hero.title: The naughty or nice quiz to take as a couple
hero.description: Has your couple been naughty or nice this year? You each answer 12 questions about your December. Then the quiz tells you which of Santa's lists you're on and who is the nicer one.
hero.subtitle: 12 questions • 3 minutes each • on a single phone

section1.title: How the quiz works
section1.p1: This quiz is a Christmas game to play as a couple. It tells you if you're on Santa's nice list or on his naughty list. To do that, it works out a niceness score as a percentage. It asks 12 questions about your December. For example, they're about the advent calendar or the last Christmas cookie, and the last one takes a look back at your year together.
section1.p2: Take the question about the presents hidden in your home. You can choose between “no snooping, the surprise comes first”, “no snooping, but the hiding place has been spotted”, “a box or two got shaken” and “everything was opened, then neatly rewrapped”. If you choose the first answer, you earn the most niceness points. If you choose the last one, you earn none.
section1.p3: The first person answers the 12 questions and then passes the phone. The second person answers without seeing what the first one chose. You each answer for yourself. At the end, the quiz averages your two scores and that gives your couple's niceness score. It also tells you who is the nicer one and which questions you're furthest apart on.
section1.p4: You can also take the quiz on your own and answer for your couple. But then you won't know who's bringing the average down!

section2.title: The 5 spots on Santa's list
section2.intro: The quiz gives you one of these five spots, depending on your niceness score. Each spot has its own photo.

section3.title: Where does the naughty or nice list come from?
section3.p1: The idea that Santa keeps a list comes mostly from a song called “Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town”. It was written by Haven Gillespie and J. Fred Coots. It was first heard on the radio in November 1934. In the song, Santa makes a list and checks it twice to find out who's naughty or nice.
section3.p2: The lump of coal is an older story. In the tradition, good children find presents in their stocking on Christmas morning and naughty children find coal. Nobody knows exactly where the custom started. What we do know is that coal was kept right next to the fireplace Santa was supposed to come down.
section3.p3: Other countries have their own version. In Italy, it's the Befana who puts coal in naughty children's stockings on the night of January 5th. In Spain, the Three Kings bring it. These days it's coal made of sugar and the children eat it! In the Netherlands, Sinterklaas keeps a big book where he writes down who has been good.

section4.title: What if you're not on the same list?
section4.p1: That's the most common case and it's also the funniest. For example, if one of you gets 80% and the other 40%, look at the questions where you're furthest apart. Most of the time, one of you wraps all the presents while the other just signs the tag. That makes a real elf and a Scrooge in the same couple.
section4.p2: Some questions are also about real life. For example: who clears the table and who thinks of presents for the whole family. If the gap doesn't make you laugh, take a look at who does what at home the rest of the year. It's often the same thing.
section4.p3: And if each of you is right at the bottom of the list, it's not a big deal. Two people who finish the box of chocolates together still make a couple that gets along.

section5.title: Good to know about this quiz
section5.p1: This quiz is a game and you shouldn't take it seriously. It says nothing about your couple. You can very well empty the advent calendar in ten days and be lovely the rest of the year.
section5.p2: Your answers aren't saved, they stay on your phone. We only count which spot you get, to see which results come up most. Your name isn't saved either. The photos were created for this page.

seo.faq1Q: How do we know if we're on the naughty or nice list?
seo.faq1A: Just take the quiz together. You each answer 12 questions about your December and the quiz works out your couple's niceness score. From 65%, you're on the nice list. Under 45%, you're more on the naughty list.
seo.faq2Q: How is the niceness score calculated?
seo.faq2A: Each answer is worth between 0 and 4 points. Three questions count a little more than the others: the hidden presents, dinner at the in-laws' and the year in review. The quiz then turns your total into a percentage. When you take it together, it averages your two percentages.
seo.faq3Q: Can I take the quiz on my own?
seo.faq3A: Yes. Just choose “On my own, for our couple” and answer with your couple in mind. You'll get your spot on the list but you won't know who is the nicer one.
seo.faq4Q: How do we find out who's the nicer of the two?
seo.faq4A: When you take the quiz together, it shows each person's niceness score under your couple's result. It tells you who is the nicer one and it shows you the three questions where you're furthest apart.
seo.faq5Q: Is this a naughty or nice quiz for adults or for kids?
seo.faq5A: It's for adults. The questions are written for grown-ups in a couple. For example, they're about the in-laws or the budget for presents. There's nothing shocking in it but a child won't relate to it.
seo.faq6A: No. Your answers stay on your phone. We only count which spot you get on the list, to see which results come up most, and your name isn't saved.
